correctness.rationale: The MA(2) cancellation reduces signs to two independent interlaced comparisons and produces exact reciprocal-factorial window probabilities. Overlapping events at displacement d<r are precisely a longer alternating word; d=r or r+1 share at most two innovations and obey a proved conditional rank-density bound. Arratia--Goldstein--Gordon Theorem 1 gives the fully quantified Poisson total-variation estimate with b3=0. Asymptotic error O(lambda/r+lambda^2 r^2/n), finite tail sandwich, Stirling and dyadic Borel--Cantelli yield the claimed Poisson and almost-sure limits. The included checker enumerates 1,641,300 rank permutations, including ten exact joint-overlap checks. Finite enumeration is supplementary, not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The fixed descent-pattern distribution in this equal-weight moving average follows from Bandt--Shiha Proposition 7 and is explicitly not novel. The surviving new claim is the growing-threshold quantitative Poisson approximation, its rare-overlap estimates, and the almost-sure log(n)/loglog(n) longest turning streak. The author-provided Bandt--Shiha full article and the AGG 1989 full theorem were inspected; neither states that specific result. Bender--Helton--Richmond concerns iid rise/fall words, not smoothed blocks. Searches of published records and own prior research yielded no stated or dominating equivalent. Historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: Contiguous sustained turning-point streaks are a natural oscillation-extreme summary of a filtered time series. The explicit Poisson error estimates exceedance frequencies and exposes the role of short and boundary overlap, while the almost-sure log n/loglog n scale differs qualitatively from iid alternating-word extremes. This is a model-independent-in-law structural limit across all iid atomless innovations, rather than an arbitrary enumeration or textbook finite marginal re-evaluation.
